title: Semi-free DG modules compute bimodule tensor with its target action
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Let $(A,d)$ and $(B,d)$ be such differential graded algebras. A differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodule $N$ has commuting unital graded left $A$- and right $B$-actions, with $d(an)=d(a)n+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(n)$ and $d(nb)=d(n)b+(-1)^{|n|}n\,d(b)$ for homogeneous elements. Use $T_N=-\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$ from [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction]. For $k\in\mathbf Z$ put $A[k]^i=A^{i+k}$ with differential $(-1)^kd_A$ and unchanged right action. Say that a right DG $A$-module $P$ is semi-free if it has an increasing filtration by DG submodules $0=F_{-1}P\subset F_0P\subset F_1P\subset\cdots$, with $P=\bigcup_{j\geq0}F_jP$, each inclusion split as a map of graded right $A$-modules, and each quotient $F_jP/F_{j-1}P$ isomorphic as a DG module to a small direct sum of shifts $A[k]$. For every such $P$, the canonical derived comparison is an isomorphism
$$T_N(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_A N\quad\text{in }D(B,d),$$
where the target is the balanced DG tensor of [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction], with its right $B$-action $(p\otimes n)b=p\otimes(nb)$. These comparisons are natural for DG $A$-module maps between semi-free modules: under them $T_N(f)$ is the class of $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$. This is an isomorphism of DG $B$-module objects in the derived category, not only an isomorphism of their cohomology groups or of their underlying integral complexes. No flatness over $\mathbf Z$, boundedness, countability, compactness, or condition on self extensions is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09LS, lemma-derived-bc, proof: the left derived tensor is computed on modules with property (P), as defined in section-P-resolutions; the construction takes values in D(B,d).

proof.text: Regard $A$ as the dg category with one object and endomorphism complex $A$, composition given by multiplication. Its representable right module is $A$. Reindex the given filtration by $P_0=0$ and $P_{j+1}=F_jP$. Thus its semi-free modules are precisely the modules with property (P), and [lem-coef-dg-semi-free-homotopically-projective] makes them homotopically projective. By [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived], for every such $P$ and every $X$ the localization map $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(P,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(P,X)$ is bijective.

proof.text: For every right dg module $X$, [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-resolution] gives a quasi-isomorphism $q_X:P_X\to X$ with property (P). Reindex its filtration by $F_jP_X=(P_X)_{j+1}$ to obtain exactly the semi-free filtration in the statement. All the modules and all cell sets lie in the chosen universe. Hence every object has a semi-free representative, with $Q_A(q_X)$ invertible in $D(A,d)$.

source.place: Tag 09LS, lemma-derived-bc, proof; Tags 09KK, section-P-resolutions, 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, 09KP, lemma-resolve, and 09KY, lemma-hom-derived.

proof.text: The balanced tensor of [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction] induces a functor $F:K(A,d)\to D(B,d)$. Explicitly, for a graded $A$-linear homotopy $h$ of degree $-1$, put $H(p\otimes n)=h(p)\otimes n$. It is balanced since $h(pa)=h(p)a$, and right $B$-linear since $H((p\otimes n)b)=h(p)\otimes nb=H(p\otimes n)b$. In $dH+Hd$ the terms involving $d_Nn$ cancel, with coefficients $(-1)^{|p|-1}+(-1)^{|p|}=0$; the remaining term is $(d h+h d)(p)\otimes n$. Thus homotopic maps give homotopic right $B$-linear tensor maps. Identities and composition are respected on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 09LS, lemma-derived-bc, proof; Tags 09KK, section-P-resolutions, 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, 09KP, lemma-resolve, and 09KY, lemma-hom-derived.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-localization-left-derived] to $C=K(A,d)$, $D=D(A,d)$, $Q=Q_A$, $H=D(B,d)$, the class of semi-free modules, and this functor $F$. Steps 1 and 2 verify its two substantive hypotheses. The resulting universal counit is an isomorphism at every semi-free $P$. Since [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction] specifies $T_N$ as the total left derived functor of this same balanced tensor, the criterion applies to its universal pair and gives the canonical comparison $T_N(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_A N$ in $D(B,d)$.

source.place: Tag 09LS, lemma-derived-bc, proof; Tags 09KK, section-P-resolutions, 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, 09KP, lemma-resolve, and 09KY, lemma-hom-derived.

proof.text: For a dg map $f:P\to P'$ between semi-free modules, counit naturality gives $\varepsilon_{P'}T_N(f)=[f\otimes\mathrm{id}_N]\varepsilon_P$. These are morphisms in $D(B,d)$ throughout: step 3 used the tensor right action and $B$-linear homotopies, and step 4 took $D(B,d)$ as its target category. Thus the claimed comparisons preserve that action and have the required naturality. The argument used no flatness, boundedness, countability, compactness or self-extension hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem semifree_bimodule_tensor_computation (A B : Algebra.{u}) [DerivedStructure A] [DerivedStructure B] (N : Bimod A B) (F : RightModule A ⥤ RightModule B) (_t : BalancedTensorModel N F) (T : Derived A ⥤ Derived B) (α : Q A ⋙ T ⟶ F ⋙ Q B) [T.IsRightKanExtension α] : (∀ (P : RightModule A), Nonempty (SemiFreeFiltration A P) → IsIso (α.app P)) ∧ (∀ (P P' : RightModule A), Nonempty (SemiFreeFiltration A P) → Nonempty (SemiFreeFiltration A P') → ∀ f : P ⟶ P', T.map ((Q A).map f) ≫ α.app P' = α.app P ≫ (Q B).map (F.map f))
lean.note: The node itself introduces semi-free filtrations; SemiFreeFiltration gives that filtration as actual DG modules, with exact quotient layers and degreewise coproducts of shifts. The theorem applies to the universal comparison of any balanced tensor model from the recorded derived-adjunction interface.
